findings.title: retryCount cleanup clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The first OR branch is limited to `method: SMS`, but the new `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch has no method filter. This SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this file increments retryCount. But the column is generic, and any other reminder flow that later uses it would have its rows silently deleted by the SMS job. The clause should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, and ideally `scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Unguarded prisma.update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without its own try/catch. If that update throws (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently so Prisma raises P2025), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler rejects, the endpoint returns a 500, and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped for that run. Previously one bad reminder only logged an error. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, so a bookkeeping failure cannot stop the batch.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message never increment retryCount
findings.body: retryCount is only incremented when `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (e.g. no `smsReminderNumber` on the booking) or the message is empty, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` check fails and nothing happens. The same applies to the earlier `continue` for a missing workflowStep or booking. Those reminders are never counted as failures, so the cron keeps re-processing them every run until `scheduledDate` passes. That is the exact behaviour the PR sets out to remove. A missing phone number is a common case of the 'invalid phone number' scenario in the description.

findings.title: Read-modify-write retryCount update is not atomic
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same count and both write count+1, so a failure is undercounted and the cutoff is delayed. Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids this and is the idiomatic form (the same applies to the catch block at line 195).

findings.title: Unindexed retryCount in an OR condition on a large table
findings.body: The delete's WHERE is now `(method AND scheduledDate) OR retryCount > 1`. The existing indexes (`[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, etc.) cannot serve the `retryCount` branch, so Postgres will likely fall back to a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run. Scoping the second branch to `method = SMS` and `scheduled = false` would let the existing index apply.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour
findings.body: The PR adds retry counting and a new deletion rule: a failed `scheduleSMS` increments retryCount, and rows with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the next run. None of this is covered by a test, including the off-by-one threshold (`gt: 1` means deletion after the second failure). A regression in the counting or the OR delete filter would go unnoticed.
